source_text.body:
Organize non-coding project work for repeated agent runs
The poster sets up Claude Cowork for non-coding work with project notes, prompts, instructions, memory notes and audit logs to repeat tasks across projects.
·
Jun 11, 2026
Done with
CW
Claude Cowork
What they did
The poster had already set up a Cowork HQ with Context, Projects, Outputs, and Templates plus instructions split across account, Cowork, and project levels. In the thread, experienced users explain a repeatable setup: keep broad preferences in global/Cowork settings, put the main operating instructions in an HQ-level CLAUDE.md, add workstation- or project-specific CLAUDE.md files only where needed, and use MEMORY.md or local folders to hold chat history, status, and active files; one commenter says beginners can stay in Cowork’s built-in instruction fields and migrate later.
How it went
The thread presents this as a workable way to route repeated non-coding work and keep context separated by area, but it offers no measured results. The main limitation discussed is complexity: too many folders, files, and rule layers can become confusing, especially for beginners.
Worth knowing
One practical catch: one commenter keeps a separate backup folder for Claude artifacts, schedules, and skills so the setup can be reused or moved to another model later.
Try it yourself
with
Claude Cowork
Copy prompt
Help me set up a reusable workspace for [type of non-coding project, e.g. client reports] so I can repeat the same tasks across projects. Create a folder structure with project notes, a reusable prompt file, standing instructions, a memory notes file, and an audit log that records what you did on each run. When finished, walk me through how to start a new project from it, and ask before deleting or overwriting any existing files.
Original source: https://www.reddit.com/r/ClaudeCowork/comments/1u2ovrz/claudemd_or_not
